judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives under the same Theme (Number and Numeration) and Sub-Theme (Whole Number), though in different Topics (3. Whole numbers 6-9 vs 4. Whole number 10). First objective is arranging numbers 6-9 by magnitude/quantity; second is using the idea of place value limited to tens and units. These are coherent, complementary whole-number number-sense skills but distinct in concept, and both sit at the same canonical rank (rank 0, PRIMARY ONE). There is no substantive same-rank evidence that ordering 6-9 developmentally supports place value understanding; token/hierarchy/page overlaps are generic ('pupil','should','of','the') and organizer-driven. Meaningful conceptual coherence without justified dependency supports relatesTo.

judgment.rationale: Second SFI (PRIMARY ONE, rank 0, Topic 3. Addition) is 'cross-check the correctness of addition in everyday life'; first SFI (PRIMARY TWO, rank 1, Topic 2. Subtraction) is 'apply addition and subtraction in everyday activities.' Both objectives concern the everyday-life application of addition, with the P1 objective focused on verifying addition correctness and the P2 objective broadening to applying both addition and subtraction in everyday activities. Proficiency in checking/using addition in everyday contexts plausibly supports the later, broader everyday application task, and the direction runs lower-to-higher (PRIMARY ONE -> PRIMARY TWO), matching the only permitted developmental direction. Numbering, hierarchy, and lexical overlap alone were not treated as decisive; the substantive everyday-addition coherence and cross-grade progression justify buildsTowards.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives under the same Topic 'Whole numbers 6-9' (Sub-Theme Whole Number, Theme Number and Numeration). The second SFI (obj 1: 'sort and classify numbers of objects in a group or collection') is a pre-number organizing skill that supports the first SFI (obj 2: 'identify number of objects in a group or collection'): grouping and classifying objects prepares the learner to determine how many are in a group. This is a coherent same-rank developmental support, with the source objective sequence (1 then 2) consistent with that direction. Shared LC/text token overlap and hierarchy alone do not drive this; the skill relationship does. Rank gap is 0 (both PRIMARY ONE), so confidence is moderate rather than high.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary One Performance Objectives under the same Topic '1. Three dimensional shapes' (Sub-Theme Shapes, Theme Mensuration and Geometry), at the same Grade rank (PRIMARY ONE). The second SFI (objective 2: 'identify and name cuboids, cubes, cylinders and spheres') establishes recognition and naming of the specific 3D shapes, which supports the more discriminating skill in the first SFI (objective 3: 'distinguish between cuboids and cubes'). Distinguishing between two named shapes presupposes the ability to identify and name them, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first. Source objective numbering (2 before 3) is consistent with this direction but the developmental judgment rests on the substantive skill relationship, not numbering, proximity, or shared LC tokens ('3d','shapes','cubes','cuboids') alone.
